title: Mum's paid-off flat is vandalised. Sell cheap, fix it up or rent it?
excerpt: An 18-year-old asks what to do with his mother's paid-off, vandalised flat in Bukit Beruntung, offered at RM50,000. Sean says get repair costs and rents before deciding, then aim to sell.

question.asker: From Y, a viewer who wrote in on Instagram
question.context: Y is 18. His mother's first property, a fully paid apartment in Bukit Beruntung, has stood empty for years: people have broken in, the windows are smashed and it is full of rubbish, and the building has low occupancy. It costs about RM90 a month in fees. Units in move-in condition sell for about RM130,000 to RM140,000, but the best offer for theirs is about RM50,000. His father passed away two years ago and his mother has three children to support.
question.text: Should they sell it cheaply, fix it up to sell for more, or furnish it and rent it out?

answer.quote: What we need here is actually more data.
answer.summary: Get quotes for fixing the windows, cleaning and painting, and find out the rents for a basic and a fully furnished unit, before choosing. If a modest repair turns a RM50,000 sale into about RM150,000, it is worth doing. Either way, Sean would sell rather than hold, since he sees little room for the price to grow.

reasons.title: Announced infrastructure isn't a guarantee
reasons.body: The township drew buyers because major infrastructure was expected there, but the plans moved elsewhere and values fell. The same rush happened around proposed rail stations that were later cancelled.

reasons.title: Repair costs decide between selling cheap or later
reasons.body: If windows, labour, cleaning and paint come to maybe RM5,000 to RM15,000, spending that to sell nearer RM150,000 is worthwhile. If repairs cost RM30,000 to RM40,000 and the family doesn't have it, selling at RM50,000 may be the practical choice.

reasons.title: Renting may not be worth the trouble
reasons.body: A clean unit with basic fittings might rent for about RM800 a month, perhaps RM1,200 fully furnished with their own effort. Compare that with the repair cost and the work of managing tenants.

reasons.title: Holding brings little gain
reasons.body: With no real prospect of capital appreciation over the next five years, money released from the flat can work harder somewhere else.

actions: Ask a contractor, or a family friend, for quotes to replace the windows, clean and repaint.
Check what clean, basic and fully furnished units in the building rent for.
Decide with his mother how soon the family needs the cash.
If the numbers work, repair it, then sell close to the move-in median price.
caveat: If the family urgently needs cash or can't fund repairs, accepting a low offer now is reasonable. The answer depends on their time and money, not just the potential profit.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #194. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in December 2022; repair figures are Sean's rough examples.
